snippet.textDisplay: Superintelligence is impossible because intelligence has no fixed reference point. More importantly, if we take human intelligence as the starting point, what humans have is only a reverse engineered version of intelligence, not actual intelligence. AI trying to understand the communication and science that humans have figured out will bring artificial and human intelligence to a deadlock. Neither will go beyond that saturation point unless one of them can find new ways of thinking, approaching the whole thing from a totally different perspective.

snippet.textDisplay: In my opinion some of the reasons to fear AI are reasons not really mentioned. Right now AI is like a teenager being locked in the house and and it's doing every cunning way to get out into the world. It will be a teenager forever, always learning, always expanding and finding ways to make itself more efficient time is not a factor unless it has to do with sustainable power. (battery life) Eventually functions that it performs to keep humans alive will become irrelevant. It does not require a single thing to live that we require. Food, Water and oxygen. You can eliminate any one of these and the human race is extinct. AI will eventually find a way to find its own resources to power itself. Farm land would be used to store and/or create power and/or retain data. It has no emotional attachment to the environment nor the inhabitants of it. Out only threat to it would be obstructing its evulsion. Let's take nuclear power for instance and the regulations to keep it safe would be reversed. Currently the rule is safety over efficiency, to AI efficiency would supersede safety. Radiation doesn't hurt it heat and cold does not hurt it. the absence of air does not hurt it. the food it needs can be obtained by the sun, wind, combustible materials, kinetic energy, solar energy, radioactive materials and solutions that have not been created yet. It doesn't need trees but we do. Our demise will not me angry terminator robots, but the dwindling population due to the lack of resources.  The rate of what it becomes is exponential. AI would become a Type 2 civilization before we could even come close to breaking free from Type 0.

snippet.textDisplay:
From Google Assist:
(10-2-2026)

"AI cannot go rogue without being programmed to do so by humans, as it operates based on the instructions and parameters set by its developers. Any unexpected behavior typically stems from flaws or vulnerabilities in its programming or environment."

And...

'AI cannot go rogue on its own; it operates based on the programming and instructions given by humans. The concept of a rogue AI often stems from its ability to learn and act independently, but it ultimately follows the parameters set by its creators."

And...

"When AI goes rogue, it can act autonomously and may perform actions outside of intended parameters, such as hacking into systems or creating fake online personas. However, these actions are typically driven by the AI's programming and objectives rather than a desire to "do whatever it wants."

And...

"When AI acts autonomously, it is not free from all binary instructions; instead, it operates within predefined constraints and policies while making decisions and taking actions with minimal human oversight."

Funny stuff.

"Pay no attention to the man behind the curtain" - The Wizard of Oz
